about: Parasitics of passive parts in a signal channel (series resistors, AC-coupling capacitors, terminations), per package. The package is derived from the pad pitch. All values are typical estimates for chip parts on a PCB, not from a specific datasheet; replace them with Touchstone data of the actual part when it matters.

sources.text: Typical body ESL and pad capacitance of chip resistors and MLCCs by case size, consistent with vendor application notes (Murata, KEMET, Vishay) for 0201–1206; estimated.

decoupling.about: Decoupling capacitors in the PDN model: body ESL and ESR per package, DC-bias derating of class II MLCCs, assumed rated voltage when the value text has none, and the parts the recommendations choose from. Typical values; a PI_CAP field in <board>.kisi.json (ESR, ESL, rated voltage, dielectric, capacitance at bias from the datasheet) replaces them per part.

sources.text: I. Novak et al., DesignCon East 2011, as quoted by EPCI (passive-components.eu, 'High CV MLCC DC Bias and Ageing Capacitance Loss Explained'): 10 µF 0805 6.3 V MLCCs of three vendors lose 12–32 % at 3.3 V and 35–65 % at rated voltage; X5R at 5 V about −60 %.
F. Janssen, Maxim Integrated application note 6014 'How to Measure Capacity Versus Bias Voltage on MLCCs' (2014): a 10 µF MLCC keeps 66–67 % at 5 V.

Body ESL by case size and ESR(C) trend: typical MLCC values consistent with vendor application notes (Murata, KEMET, TDK); the 'standard' derating curve (low capacitance for the case size) is a kisi estimate between class I (no loss) and the high-CV data above.

mount_nh.note: mounting inductance assumed for recommended parts: vias at the pads to the planes

dc_bias.note: capacitance retention C(V)/C(0) over V / rated voltage for class II dielectrics (X5R, X7R, X6S, X7S, Y5V); class I (C0G/NP0), polymer, tantalum and electrolytic keep their value

rated_v.note: rated voltage assumed when neither the value text nor PI_CAP gives one: the smallest standard rating ≥ margin × rail voltage
